sources.citation: Ezard, Bryan. 1997. A grammar of Tawala: an Austronesian language of the Milne Bay area, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-137. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Describes TAWALA (tawa1275), not Wagawaga. Table 1 (p.6) lists Yaleba (alternate names 'Wagawaga, Gwawili, Gwavili, Ealeba') as a Tawala dialect; p.7 explains Ray 1938 gave two 'Wagawaga' wordlists, one Tawala-like and one a separate (Suauic) language. Sec. 4.5 (p.44): 'Stress in Tawala is predictable, occurring on the penultimate (second to last) syllable.' with secondary stress on alternate syllables leftward. Relevant only to the Yaleba [ylb] half of the retired code, and belongs in the catalog under tawa1275.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David R. 1976. Austronesian languages: Milne Bay and adjacent islands (Milne Bay Province). In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 2: Austronesian Languages, 441-523. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 36 (p.457) defines 'Wagawaga' as spoken on the SW shore of Milne Bay (Kilakilana, Gamadoudou, Wagawaga) AND at the eastern tip (Kanakope, Noabune, Simagahi) = the old wgw scope. Sec. 84 'Stress' (p.475) is cluster-wide only: 'In all of the languages of PTC it seems that stress is predictable within certain word-classes, notably kinship nouns and verbs' with stress moving one syllable toward the end under suffixation; phonemic stress named only for Kilivila, Muyuw, Budibud, Misima (prob. Nimowa, Sud-Est). Nothing specific to Wagawaga.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2009. Change Request Number 2009-045 (submitted by Sara Van Cott, SIL PNG): split [wgw] into Wagawaga [wgb] and Yaleba [ylb], effective 2010-01-18. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; administrative form. Rationale: 66-76% lexical similarity, marginal intelligibility, no shared identity; based on a 2005 SIL PNG survey of Yaleba, Wagawaga and Oya'oya.
